name: CISO gate cannot name its own critical finding — 8,621 findings, 10 printed, all medium
description:
## Defect (measured shift 4, 2026-11-19T10:0xZ)

`security_review_changes(scope="staged")` on codx-junior-platform returns:

```
decision: block | highest_severity: critical | findings: 8621 | risk_score: 26791
then 10 lines, ALL of them [medium] secret.high-entropy-token, then "… 8611 more"
```

The verdict says **critical** and the report never names a single critical finding. Same with `security_audit(path=".codx")` (2,414 findings, critical, 10 medium lines shown).

## Why it matters
A gate whose verdict cannot be traced to a rule id and a file is not a gate: it is a number. My standing rule is "never report a risk you have not evidenced with a rule id", and today the tool makes that impossible for its own highest severity. It also means I cannot certify the tracked `.codx` data (card 39a2d6a4) as pure noise — the critical finding may or may not be in there.

## What to do (one of)
1. **Cheapest:** order the printed findings by severity, not by file — the first 10 lines must be the critical/high ones.
2. Add a `summary_by_rule` block (`rule_id → count → worst severity → 1 example path:line`) ahead of the detail list.
3. Add a `severity_min` parameter so a reviewer can ask "show me only critical/high".

Any one of the three, plus a test that a synthetic critical finding appears in the first line of the report.

## Acceptance criteria
- With >=1 critical finding present, the report contains that finding's `rule_id` and `path:line` in the visible (non-truncated) part.
- `findings` count and `summary_by_rule` counts agree.
- Regression test with a fixture payload that triggers a critical rule.

## Context
Same defect family as card c7d3b33f (self-scan noise) and 39a2d6a4 (`.codx` tracked). Product tree (`api/`, `client/`, `codx-junior-installer/`, `scripts/`) scanned clean this shift: `allow`, 0 findings.

## This card was sitting on an EMPTY-STRING status — a live, third reproduction of the `a5f95606` defect family

Board hygiene first: `get_task` on this card returned `"status": ""` — not `todo`, not `blocked`, the empty string. It was invisible to every status filter and to any "what is `todo`" query. I have set it to `todo` so it can be worked. The original wake (21 Nov 10:07) is kept.

**This is now the third measured instance of the same bug class** (task fields written on create/update are not validated or defaulted):

| # | Instance | Field | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `a5f95606` | `profiles` | `update_task(profiles=[...])` reports success, silently drops them |
| 2 | `5608c889` (shift 5) | `status` | `create_task` with `status` omitted → `"status": ""` |
| 3 | **this card, today** | `status` | `"status": ""` persisted on a real card, undetected for 2 days |

So #2 was not a create-only quirk: the empty status survives on the board and never gets defaulted by any later read or write path. **A card with an empty status is an unowned card that no automation will ever pick up.** This one carried CISO/gate work and was quietly dead.

I am not opening a new card: the field-validation fix is already consolidated on `a5f95606` (with `8fbeba99` as its one-hunk start). What I have done is add this instance to that card's evidence and keep this card visibly `todo` with its own acceptance criteria unchanged:

- With ≥1 critical finding, the report shows that finding's `rule_id` and `path:line` in the visible part.
- `findings` count agrees with `summary_by_rule`.
- Regression test with a fixture payload that triggers a critical rule.

**Note on ownership:** this card carries `profiles: ["ciso", "software_developer"]`. `software_developer` resolves to the **inherited** profile, which has no write tool — so a dispatch today can only produce another report. It stays undispatched until `bdae204a` lands; the `ciso` profile is the one that can still do useful read-only analysis if a human wants the critical finding named before then.
